author: mkb79
body:
Second finding from the live release of #878, after the 404-handling fix of #879 worked as designed and failed closed on something new: the narrowed app token got **403 "Resource not accessible by integration"** on the REST ref lookup — while git-protocol access with the same token (the release-pr checkout) worked. Most repository REST endpoints sit behind **metadata: read**, which an unnarrowed installation token carries implicitly and our `permission-contents`-only narrowing dropped.

Two changes, each sufficient alone:

- the lookup now uses the workflow's own read token — the read must keep working even when something is wrong with the app, because it is what tells a retried run whether the state it sees is its own earlier progress; only the *create* needs the app
- the mint requests `permission-metadata: read` explicitly, so the app token can use REST reads again

State remains clean and verified: no tag, PyPI 404. **Heal path after merging:** re-run the failed jobs of run 29986832144 — outputs and the built artifact of the green jobs are preserved, so the release resumes at the tag.

## 요약
opacity_rank 순수 코어(#12, main `610da18`)를 **DB에 배선**하는 척추. washing_flag 대체의 저장·계산·서빙 3층을 mna 형제 패턴으로 세운다.

## 저장 결정 — mna 옆(파티 결정 2026-07-23)
`opacity_rank`는 mna_target_score와 같은 **cross-sectional 백분위**다. 세대가 섞이면 순위표 자체가 무의미해지므로, washing_flag처럼 valueup_score(종목별 절대 측정치, 종목별 커밋)에 컬럼으로 얹지 않고 **별도 원자성 테이블** `opacity_score`로 둔다.

## 조각
- **마이그 0014 + `OpacityScore` 모델** — mna_score 형제(id, corp_code, as_of, opacity_rank, opacity_count, opacity_basis). uq(corp,as_of).
- **`app/repositories/opacity_score.py`** — `all_latest_plans` 배치(disclosure_date look-ahead) + upsert/delete/latest_as_of.
- **`opacity_engine.run`** — 전량 원자성 + 실패 보고(mna와 동일 정책). 모집단은 **밸류업 계획을 공시한 종목뿐** — 미참여·표지 통지문은 최대 불투명으로 벌하지 않고 행을 만들지 않는다(레아 원칙: "약속 안 한 걸 드러낸다, 못 낸 걸 벌하지 않는다").
- **run_scoring CLI** — opacity를 순위 기반 엔진으로 배선(mna와 함께 `publishable` 게이트, `--engine opacity`, 기본 `all`=셋).
- **`list_screening` 3번째 outer join** — opacity_rank·opacity_count·opacity_basis·has_opacity_score 서빙 + opacity_rank 정렬 화이트리스트. `latest_as_of`도 3테이블로 확장.

## 배선 실증 (라이브 HTTP, 프론트 DoD)
임시 DB로 엔진→DB→조인→서빙 전 스택 관통:
- `GET /screening?sort=-opacity_rank` → opacity_rank `1.0→0.5→0.0` 내림차순, `basis=market_fallback`(3종목 < peer_min 5 → small-N 시장 폴백) 와이어 반환.
- opacity만 있는 종목(has_valueup=false·has_mna=false·has_opacity=true)도 서빙 확인(신규 OR 분기).
- **실증이 잡은 버그**: `latest_as_of`가 opacity_score를 안 봐 opacity만 최근인 세대가 빈 결과를 내던 문제 → 수정.

## 테스트
- 백엔드 **311 그린**(코어 14 + 엔진 배선 5 + 서빙 3 + CLI 정합 유지).
- 마이그레이션 전체 체인 0014까지 임시 DB 적용 검증, DDL↔모델 일치.

author: kphutt
body:
Gives this repo the same local-check baseline as the rest of the fleet, per the fleet-wide tiering rule and process in my shared conventions.

## What this adds

A **pinned** secret scan via the upstream gitleaks hook:

```yaml
- repo: https://github.com/gitleaks/gitleaks
  rev: v8.30.1
  hooks: [{id: gitleaks}]
```

`language: golang` means **pre-commit builds the binary itself** — no local install, no "whatever version happens to be on PATH", and `rev:` pins it so two machines can't silently run different detection rules.

This replaces the shared `core.hooksPath` shim, which pointed every repo at one hook directory on one machine. That design was superseded fleet-wide (in a separate PR, closed unmerged) in favour of self-contained per-repo configs — so a **clone** gets the checks, rather than a **machine** having them.

## Verified, not assumed

- Config runs clean here (`pre-commit run --all-files`)
- The hook **blocks**: a planted high-entropy token produced `Failed`, exit 1
- Hooks installed and firing: `pre-commit` + `pre-push`

## Install

```sh
pre-commit install --hook-type pre-commit --hook-type pre-push
```

This repo has no test or lint suite to mirror, so the secret scan is the whole local gate — which is also all the previous shared hook provided.

- Rep-detection is not reliable enough to gate workout progression, so timed intervals must be authoritative while leaving camera/pose feedback optional and non-blocking.

author: copilot
body:
`libMOOSGeodesy` had no SOVERSION, so `dpkg-shlibdeps` couldn't resolve it to a package, and `moos-ivp-apps` (which links against it) never got an automatic `Depends: libmoos-ivp`.

## Root cause
- `libMOOS` already had a SOVERSION patch (`core-moos-01-add-soversion`), but `libMOOSGeodesy` did not.
- Without a SONAME, `dh_makeshlibs` generates no shlibs entry, so `dh_shlibdeps` can't map `moos-ivp-apps`'s `NEEDED libMOOSGeodesy.so` back to `libmoos-ivp`.

## Fix
- **New patch `geodesy-moos-01-add-soversion`**: adds `set_target_properties(${LIBNAME} PROPERTIES VERSION "1" SOVERSION "1")` to `MOOSGeodesy/libMOOSGeodesy/CMakeLists.txt`, mirroring the existing `libMOOS` fix.
- **Split `.install` files**: the new versioned `libMOOSGeodesy.so.1` goes to the runtime `libmoos-ivp` package; the unversioned `.so` symlink (link-time only) moves to `libmoos-ivp-dev`, matching the existing `libmoos10-mit`/`libmoos10-mit-dev` convention.
- **Changelog**: bumped to `24.8.1+dfsg-2`.

```
# libmoos-ivp.install
usr/lib/lib*.a
usr/lib/lib*.so.*

# libmoos-ivp-dev.install
usr/include/ivp/*
usr/include/MOOS/*
usr/lib/lib*.so
```

Result: `moos-ivp-apps`'s generated `Depends:` now includes `libmoos-ivp (>= 24.8.1+dfsg)`.

author: tobby168
body:
## Purpose

When a value in `compile_sizes` would be changed by cudagraph padding, `CudagraphDispatcher._compute_bs_to_padded_graph_size` (in `vllm/v1/cudagraph_dispatcher.py`) raises:

```
compile_sizes contains 1 which would be padded to 3. All compile_sizes must be
values that won't be changed by cudagraph padding. Use values from cudagraph_capture_sizes.
```

This is hard to act on, and **actively misleading under speculative decoding**. With MTP / `num_speculative_tokens=2`, `adjust_cudagraph_sizes_for_spec_decode` rounds the capture sizes up to a multiple of `(num_speculative_tokens + 1)`, so the configured sizes `[1, 2, 4, 8, ...]` become `[3, 6, 12, 24, ...]`. A user who follows the advice and picks a value from the *originally configured* `cudagraph_capture_sizes` (e.g. `1`) hits the same error again. The function already computes the exact valid values in its padding map but doesn't surface them.

## Changes

Improve the `ValueError` to:
1. State the padded value the offending size maps to (kept, clarified).
2. List the **actual valid `compile_sizes`**, derived from the padding map the function already computes (the fixed points), truncated for readability when there are many capture sizes.
3. Explain the spec-decode rounding as the reason when speculative decoding is enabled.

Example new message under spec decode:

```
compile_sizes contains 1 which would be padded to 3 by cudagraph padding. All
compile_sizes must be values that won't be changed by padding. Valid compile_sizes
are: [3, 6, 12, 24]. Speculative decoding is enabled, so cudagraph capture sizes
are rounded up to a multiple of (num_speculative_tokens + 1); the valid compile_sizes
therefore differ from the originally configured cudagraph_capture_sizes.
```

## Test

Extends the existing `tests/compile/test_config.py::test_compile_sizes_padding_validation` to assert the new message content, including a speculative-decoding case (capture sizes `[3, 6, 12, 24]`, `compile_sizes=[1]`) that asserts the valid-sizes list and the spec-decode explanation are present.

Message-only / validation-message change; no behavior change to padding or dispatch.

author: kphutt
body:
Gives this repo the same local-check baseline as the rest of the fleet, per the fleet-wide tiering rule and process in my shared conventions.

## What this adds

A **pinned** secret scan via the upstream gitleaks hook:

```yaml
- repo: https://github.com/gitleaks/gitleaks
  rev: v8.30.1
  hooks: [{id: gitleaks}]
```

`language: golang` means **pre-commit builds the binary itself** — no local install, no "whatever version happens to be on PATH", and `rev:` pins it so two machines can't silently run different detection rules.

This replaces the shared `core.hooksPath` shim, which pointed every repo at one hook directory on one machine. That design was superseded fleet-wide (in a separate PR, closed unmerged) in favour of self-contained per-repo configs — so a **clone** gets the checks, rather than a **machine** having them.

## Verified, not assumed

- Config runs clean here (`pre-commit run --all-files`)
- The hook **blocks**: a planted high-entropy token produced `Failed`, exit 1
- Hooks installed and firing: `pre-commit` + `pre-push`

## Install

```sh
pre-commit install --hook-type pre-commit --hook-type pre-push
```

This repo has no test or lint suite to mirror, so the secret scan is the whole local gate — which is also all the previous shared hook provided.

body:
## Review Fast Path

- User path fixed: Jarvis app update -> managed Gog repair -> Google Workspace token access keeps the upstream code requirement instead of prompting repeatedly.
- Proof: 50 targeted tests pass locally; clean macOS CI downloaded the pinned 0.33.0 assets and verified checksums, both architectures, strict signatures, identifier `com.steipete.gogcli.gog`, and Team `Y5PE65HELJ`.
- Shared-state footgun removed: packaging no longer destroys Gog signatures with `lipo` and Jarvis re-signing; startup repairs an already-installed same-version drifted copy without touching Keychain items.
- Still hurts: this Mac has broken certificate trust evaluation (`CSSMERR_TP_NOT_TRUSTED` even for Apple system binaries), so the decisive real-signature proof came from the clean macOS CI runner.

## Why This Matters

- macOS Keychain ACLs bind Gog tokens to its designated code requirement. Re-signing Gog as Jarvis makes existing tokens treat it as a different application.
- Keeping pinned vendor-signed slices avoids token deletion, OAuth changes, reauthentication, and global Homebrew mutation.

## Scope Boundary

- Packages the official signed arm64 and x86_64 Gog 0.33.0 binaries separately.
- Fails closed on checksum, architecture, signature, identifier, Team ID, version, or license drift.
- Allows mixed-team signing only for the two exact Gog runtime paths; all other native payloads retain the Jarvis same-team requirement.
- Startup atomically replaces a same-version managed Gog when its bytes differ from the packaged copy.
- Does not inspect or modify Keychain items, Google Cloud settings, OAuth tokens, accounts, or the live Jarvis runtime.

## Verification

- `bash -n scripts/package-mac-app.sh scripts/codesign-mac-app.sh scripts/verify-consumer-mac-app.sh scripts/lib/openclaw-runtime-payloads.sh scripts/lib/consumer-gog-runtime.sh scripts/test-gog-vendor-signature.sh scripts/verify-gog-release-artifacts.sh`
- `bash scripts/test-gog-vendor-signature.sh`
- `pnpm test -- test/scripts/gog-vendor-signature.test.ts src/infra/startup-reconciler.test.ts src/scripts/ci-changed-scope.test.ts` (24 tests)
- `pnpm test -- test/scripts/consumer-product-rename.test.ts test/scripts/consumer-runtime-version.test.ts test/scripts/jarvis-consumer-rc-package.test.ts test/scripts/consumer-capabilities-manifest.test.ts` (26 tests)
- `pnpm exec oxlint ...` passed for changed TS/JS files.
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check ...` passed for changed formatted files.
- Clean macOS CI passed the pinned-release signature gate, Swift lint, release build, and Swift tests.
- Both full Node test shards, install smoke, actionlint, CI-scope tests, startup-memory, protocol, channels, extensions, and Bun checks passed.
- `pnpm check` fails only on two unrelated pre-existing TypeScript errors in `src/browser/routes/agent.existing-session.test.ts`: missing `jsdom` declarations and a `Promise<unknown>`/`Promise<boolean>` mismatch. This PR does not modify that file.

## Risks and Mitigations

- Risk: upstream rotates Gog signing identity.
  - Mitigation: packaging pins the exact identifier and Team ID and fails closed.
- Risk: mixed-team code is accidentally broadened.
  - Mitigation: the exception matches only `openclaw/tools/gog/darwin-arm64/gog` and `darwin-x86_64/gog`; regression tests reject other paths.
- Risk: current same-version Jarvis copy is never healed.
  - Mitigation: startup compares packaged and managed bytes and replaces drift atomically.

## Failure Recovery

- Revert this commit and ship the previous package layout. No Keychain rollback or token migration is required because this change never edits token data.

## AI Assistance

- AI-assisted
- Testing degree: targeted locally plus clean-host macOS signature, Swift, and full Node CI proof

Gives this repo the same local-check baseline as the rest of the fleet, per the fleet-wide tiering rule and process in my shared conventions.

## What this adds

A **pinned** secret scan via the upstream gitleaks hook:

```yaml
- repo: https://github.com/gitleaks/gitleaks
  rev: v8.30.1
  hooks: [{id: gitleaks}]
```

`language: golang` means **pre-commit builds the binary itself** — no local install, no "whatever version happens to be on PATH", and `rev:` pins it so two machines can't silently run different detection rules.

This replaces the shared `core.hooksPath` shim, which pointed every repo at one hook directory on one machine. That design was superseded fleet-wide (in a separate PR, closed unmerged) in favour of self-contained per-repo configs — so a **clone** gets the checks, rather than a **machine** having them.

- Hooks installed and firing: `pre-commit` + `pre-push`

```sh
pre-commit install --hook-type pre-commit --hook-type pre-push
```

This repo has no test or lint suite to mirror, so the secret scan is the whole local gate — which is also all the previous shared hook provided.

author: avatarsd
body:
## The dead-web-ui bug

A composed-root READ (`read_subtree_folded`, RFC-0005 §C) serves a folded ~hundreds-of-links snapshot. The fold path is fully nothrow-guarded (it soft-fails `BACKPRESSURE` on every allocation), **but it can SUCCEED and then the reply builder's own link-table reserve fail** — a second large contiguous block, one link larger than the fold's, on an already-fragmented heap.

`op_resolver_t::resolve`'s success sites returned that empty rope, and `fwd_router_t`'s `if (reply->link_count() == 0) return;` guard (`fwd_router.cpp:355/382`) dropped it with **no reply at all**. A WebSocket client read the missing reply as a dead session (no reply within its prime deadline) and churned **teardown + redial** — each redial re-primed the *same* failing composed snapshot and re-failed, so the page stayed wedged. That churn also fed the dead-peer accounting.

The asymmetry that hid it: an OOM *inside* `read_subtree_folded` already returns an addressed `BACKPRESSURE` (`op_resolve_walk.hpp` `if (!r) return assemble_error(...)`); an OOM in the *reply assembly* dropped silently.

## The fix (`core/src/op_resolve_walk.hpp`)

1. **`assemble`**: on a head-segment alloc failure, `return rope_t{}` instead of falling through to append the shared payload views — those views *without* the FWD header are a headerless, unroutable frame that the send site's `link_count() > 0` guard would wave through as garbage.
2. **`or_backpressure`** (new): an empty (OOM) success reply becomes an addressed `STATUS{ ERROR{ VALUE tr::flow::backpressure (0x0040) } }` reply — a shape the WS client already handles, so it falls back on the **same** link instead of tearing down. The error tail's only allocation is a 14-byte head segment (`try_reserve(1)` is the inline fast path), so it succeeds on exactly the fragmented heap that could not reserve the snapshot's link table.
3. Wrap all five READ / WRITE / AWAIT / `:subscribers[]` success sites in `or_backpressure`.

Non-OOM replies are byte-identical.

## Test

`graph_oom_softfail_test` gains `test_composed_read_reply_backpressure`: a 40-child composed-root READ with `fail_exact` targeting **exactly** the reply's link-table reserve (`(1 + fold_links) * sizeof(view_t)` — `heap_alloc` bypasses the probe hook, so that reserve is the only injectable reply allocation; the fold's own reserve is one link smaller and its node/stack growths a different element size). Verified it **fails without the wrap** (reply is a silently-dropped `link_count()==0` rope → all 4 assertions fail) and passes with it.

- Full `core/` host suite: **57/57 green**
- ASan (subtree, subtree_snapshot, graph_oom_softfail, graph, op_resolve, op_resolve_view): green
- TSan (graph_oom_softfail, graph, op_resolve, op_resolve_view): green
- `clang-format` 18.1.8 clean
- CHANGELOG updated

## Relationship to the retirement work

This is the leanness prerequisite (peak/contiguous-heap pressure) before the legacy-stack retirement slices in a private downstream integration; it also starves the redial churn that fed the dead-peer leak hunt.

Advances the Linux cross-platform migration (#27) through **Phase 0 + Phase 1**, all Windows-buildable and additive — the WinUI app, shim, and CI are untouched; WinUI remains the shipping Windows build until the Linux native pipeline exists.

## Phase 0 — foundation + decision
- **Design spec** `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-23-linux-cross-platform-design.md` — decision, grounded research (5 parallel agents, sources inline), reuse map, phased roadmap, 3 gating spikes.
- **`src/CameraOnScreen.App.Avalonia`** scaffold referencing `Core`, added to the solution.
- Proved the MVVM view models (already in `Core`, `CommunityToolkit.Mvvm`, no WinUI types) reuse across toolkits with **no extraction**.
- Pinned **net8 + Avalonia 11.2.1** (template default net10/Avalonia 12 has a Roslyn-4.14 source generator that silently no-ops on SDK 8).

## Phase 1 — full control-panel parity
- Ported **every control** from `src/CameraOnScreen.App/MainWindow.xaml` to Avalonia, bound to the reused `MainViewModel`: camera picker + Start/Stop + status line, Mirror, exposure lock/slider, AI Green Screen + expand/feather, Eye Contact + note, AI Sharpness + Quality, Smooth 60fps (FRUC), Hand grab + sensitivity, capability notes, Maxine attribution footer.
- WinUI `x:Bind` function helpers -> Avalonia converters (`Converters.cs`): `StatusLineConverter`, `AllTrueConverter`, `QualityEnabledConverter`; `!available` visibilities use `{Binding !Prop}`; attribution via `{x:Static core:AppInfo.MaxineAttribution}`.
- Deliberate Phase 1 simplifications tracked in **#29** (theme-neutral brushes, FakeShim demo DataContext, no persistence/overlay wiring yet — all Phase 2+).

## Decision (full rationale in the spec)
Avalonia + native C-ABI shim (`.so`), keep Maxine. Electron/Tauri rejected — a web framework only replaces the control panel once Maxine is kept, and Avalonia reuses the existing C# where they would not; Tauri additionally disqualified on Linux (WebKitGTK getUserMedia off by default, Wayland always-on-top no-ops).

## Test
```
dotnet build src/CameraOnScreen.App.Avalonia   # 0 warnings / 0 errors
dotnet run  --project src/CameraOnScreen.App.Avalonia   # full panel; controls bound to the VM
```
Verified on Windows (SDK 8.0.423): clean build, launch with no binding errors. The project is cross-platform net8 — the same `dotnet run` is the intended first smoke test on the new Linux box (proves Avalonia/X11 works there before any native work).

Phase 2+ native work and the 3 Linux+RTX de-risk spikes (Maxine gaze in-process, X11 transparent overlay captured live, per-OS CUDA/TRT co-version) — they need a Linux+RTX box.

Companion of walkline/ToCloud9#75, which adds the two RPCs on the ToCloud9 side.

The 3.3.5 client gates its guild control buttons on those fields, so without this a promoted member keeps the old buttons until relog. It returns whether the player was found on this worldserver, so the caller can degrade cleanly. This complements #3, which rehydrates the same fields at login.

Design spec and plan: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-22-stacky-composable-stack-cli-design.md`, `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-22-stacky-phase-1.md`.

### Architecture
- **`@stacky/core`** — headless: `loadRegistry` → `resolve` → `plan` → `apply`. Pure except `apply` (the only writer). Ambiguity is returned as data, never prompted — so CLI, a future web UI, and LLM agents (`--json`) all render one resolver.
- **`@stacky/cli`** — thin adapter: `init`/`add`/`remove`/`plan`/`apply`/`list`, exit codes `0`/`1`/`2` (2 = needs input), colored diff, git-dirty safety guard.

### Three-tier file ownership (what makes `remove` trustworthy)
| Tier | Section | On removal |
|---|---|---|
| brick-owned | `[[files]]` | file deleted |
| composed | `[[fragments]]` | regenerated from remaining bricks (yaml deep-merge / lines dedup) |
| marker-injected | `[[inject]]` | region emptied, host file untouched |

A `stack.toml` manifest + `stack.lock` (sha256 per file) drive convergence and drift detection.

### Acceptance gate
The round-trip property test — for every brick, `add X` → `remove X` returns the tree **byte-identical** — passes for all bricks including the Postgres inject case. Golden-file tests pin the full-stack `compose.yml` and `.env.example`. The Docker artifact test runs `docker compose config` against generated output and passes.

### Verification
- 68 tests passing, 1 skipped (caddy artifact test, skips when `caddy` absent)
- `tsc -b` clean across the workspace
- Executed via 12 spec+quality-reviewed tasks; a final whole-branch review traced the full add→remove lifecycle and found no merge-blockers

### Deferred to phase 2 (non-blocking, from the final review)
- `apply()` writes the lockfile once at end rather than per-op (spec's error-handling section promises per-op checkpointing); crash-window-only, git-recoverable.
- The `.stacky-new` conflict sidecar + `--force` are unreachable via the CLI today (the CLI returns before `apply()` on conflicts).
- Round-trip gate iterates a hardcoded brick list; derive from the registry so new bricks can't silently escape coverage.
- `bin: stacky` needs a build step to run under plain `node`.

body:
Gives this repo the same local-check baseline as the rest of the fleet, per the fleet-wide tiering rule and process in my shared conventions.

## What this adds

A **pinned** secret scan via the upstream gitleaks hook:

```yaml
- repo: https://github.com/gitleaks/gitleaks
  rev: v8.30.1
  hooks: [{id: gitleaks}]
```

`language: golang` means **pre-commit builds the binary itself** — no local install, no "whatever version happens to be on PATH", and `rev:` pins it so two machines can't silently run different detection rules.

This replaces the shared `core.hooksPath` shim, which pointed every repo at one hook directory on one machine. That design was superseded fleet-wide (in a separate PR, closed unmerged) in favour of self-contained per-repo configs — so a **clone** gets the checks, rather than a **machine** having them.

## Verified, not assumed

- Config runs clean here (`pre-commit run --all-files`)
- The hook **blocks**: a planted high-entropy token produced `Failed`, exit 1
- Hooks installed and firing: `pre-commit` + `pre-push`

## Install

```sh
pre-commit install --hook-type pre-commit --hook-type pre-push
```

This repo has no test or lint suite to mirror, so the secret scan is the whole local gate — which is also all the previous shared hook provided.

author: zacharyzcr
body:
## What

Past `index_topk` context, DSA sparse decode today forces the whole layer's attention onto the CPU: the CUDA absorb kernel only scans contiguous KV rows and cannot consume the selection list, so `attention_rows` bails (`if(dnsel[s]>0){cuda_core=0;break;}`) and long-context decode loses the GPU exactly when attention cost peaks.

`COLI_DSA_GATHER=1` closes that gap without touching the kernel: gather the DSA-selected top-k rows into a compact `[ns, kv_lora]` / `[ns, qk_rope]` staging pair on the host, and hand the existing dense `coli_cuda_attention_absorb` that. Scores, softmax, and the latent mix are position-free (RoPE is applied at KV-write time), so a dense scan over gathered rows computes the same attention the CPU gather loop does.

## Why this is the first stone of KV tiering

Host KV stays canonical; only `~index_topk` rows (≈4.7 MB at kv_lora=512) cross PCIe per (layer, token). The device never needs the full context resident — which is the read path of hot/cold KV tiering (the same shape SGLang has on its 2026 Q2 roadmap for NSA models: full KV in host memory, only the sparse top-k in device memory). The natural next steps stack on this seam: a device-side gather (index list into the kernel, feeding from a resident `kv_dev` shadow — zero PCIe), and pinned staging for true DMA.

## Correctness

- **Identity selection is byte-exact**: with `DSA_FORCE=1` at short context (selection = all positions, ascending), output is byte-identical to the dense CUDA absorb path — the staging and the call are exact.
- **Partial selection diverges only by kernel family**, which is the pre-existing contract, not a new behavior. Discrimination experiment at 2,943-token context (frozen usage snapshot, greedy): all-CPU attention, the current mixed path, and the gather path produce three *mutually different* fluent continuations — the first generated token after this near-tie-heavy prompt flips under any kernel-family change, exactly the #510 doctrine (bit-identity holds within a kernel family, not across).

## Measured (6x RTX 5090, GLM-5.2 int4, 2,943-token prompt, 32-token greedy decode)

| | decode |
|---|---|
| CPU sparse (today's fallback) | 4.08 tok/s |
| `COLI_DSA_GATHER=1` | 3.81 tok/s |

Parity-to-slightly-behind at 3k context on this box — the AVX-512 CPU sweep over 2,048 rows is already fast, and the gather pays a host memcpy + PCIe upload per layer. The value at this stage is architectural (device no longer needs full-context KV; CPU freed from the attention sweep on sparse layers) and it establishes the seam the device-side gather needs. Default off; zero behavior change unless `COLI_DSA_GATHER=1`.

author: timdebruijn
body:
The three advisory points left from the original fundamentals review.

## 1. `reboot_required` in the PATCH response

Most settings (WiFi, MQTT, Modbus, poll interval, driver, NTP) are read once at boot, so a `PATCH /api/v1/config` stores them but they only take effect after a restart. The response now carries a top-level `reboot_required` boolean so a **non-UI API client** knows whether to reboot — previously only the web UI knew, by inferring it client-side.

The decision lives in a host-tested `configChangeRequiresReboot(before, after)` in the config layer — one authoritative, complete list of boot-only vs live-applied settings. The web UI now trusts this flag as its restart trigger (keeping its nice per-field labels for the wording), so UI and API can never disagree.

**Supporting fix:** `logging.level` is now genuinely applied live (`log::setLevel` in `applyConfig`). The UI claimed "applied immediately" but it actually needed a reboot; making the claim true is cleaner than reporting it as boot-only.

## 2. MQTT username treated as a credential

`GET /api/v1/config` is unauthenticated (per the documented LAN model) and omits all passwords. The MQTT username — half of a login pair — was still returned in the clear. It's now handled exactly like its password: omitted from the API response, exposed only as `username_set`, and sent by the UI only when typed. Non-credential config (broker host, topics) stays readable. **Storage is unchanged** — `serializeConfigForStorage()` still persists the username; only the API view redacts it.

## 3. OTA signing documented as a known limitation

`security.md` now states plainly: the `0xE9` magic check rejects a wrong *file*, not malicious *firmware*. Anyone with the admin password can flash anything that boots. Signed OTA (secure boot v2) is named as the mitigation and why it's not enabled (key management, recovery, open-source build; LAN threat model).

## Verification

- `pio test -e native`: **422/422** (5 new tests — reboot classification, PATCH-only flag, username redaction)
- `tools/check_web_js.py`: OK · `check_layering.sh`: PASS
- Firmware builds: rs485-can, relay-6ch, mock — success, zero own-code warnings

author: kphutt
body:
Gives this repo the same local-check baseline as the rest of the fleet, per the fleet-wide tiering rule and process in my shared conventions.

## What this adds

A **pinned** secret scan via the upstream gitleaks hook:

```yaml
- repo: https://github.com/gitleaks/gitleaks
  rev: v8.30.1
  hooks: [{id: gitleaks}]
```

`language: golang` means **pre-commit builds the binary itself** — no local install, no "whatever version happens to be on PATH", and `rev:` pins it so two machines can't silently run different detection rules.

This replaces the shared `core.hooksPath` shim, which pointed every repo at one hook directory on one machine. That design was superseded fleet-wide (in a separate PR, closed unmerged) in favour of self-contained per-repo configs — so a **clone** gets the checks, rather than a **machine** having them.

## Verified, not assumed

- Config runs clean here (`pre-commit run --all-files`)
- The hook **blocks**: a planted high-entropy token produced `Failed`, exit 1
- Hooks installed and firing: `pre-commit` + `pre-push`

## Install

```sh
pre-commit install --hook-type pre-commit --hook-type pre-push
```

This repo has no test or lint suite to mirror, so the secret scan is the whole local gate — which is also all the previous shared hook provided.

author: lalinsky
body:
Rework of the loop's op accounting, first step of the Linux backend unification (runtime io_uring/epoll selection and later a hybrid mode).

## active

- Per-loop `std.atomic.Value(usize)` on `LoopState`, replacing the comptime split between a plain per-loop field and group-shared storage in the backend `SharedState`.
- Incremented at the loop's submit sites (backends no longer do any accounting in `submit`).
- Decremented in `finishCompletion` **routed through `completion.loop`**, the loop that owns the completion. The finish can run on a different loop's thread (epoll single-owner servicing, the shared IOCP port, and notably a group/`net_send_file` parent finished by whichever loop ran its last child) - routing keeps the counter exact in all of these with one uniform rule.
- `done()` is now per-loop: everything submitted on a loop holds that loop open, regardless of which loop services it. This is groundwork for the follow-up PR, where the epoll/kqueue park path will hand full completion custody (`completion.loop`, count included) to the fd's owner loop.

## inflight

- Removed from `LoopState` entirely; it is an internal backend optimization for skipping the poll syscall when nothing can arrive.
- Each backend counts ops it accepted in its own storage: plain field for io_uring/poll (single-threaded ownership, no atomics), group-shared atomic for epoll/kqueue/iocp (a completion can be finished by another loop of the group).
- The loop asks `backend.hasInflight()` in `tick` and tells the backend to drop one via the `decrInflight` hook in `markCompletedFromBackend`.

## Removed

- `BackendCapabilities.is_multi_threaded` - it conflated "where does active live" with "where does inflight live"; both questions now have per-backend answers and the flag has no readers left.

## Side effect

`recomputeShedQuota` now compares per-loop active counts instead of inflight. On backends where inflight was group-shared, every executor read the same value (`mine == avg` always), so load shedding was silently inert there; per-loop counts make it meaningful. The uniform +1 baseline from each executor's shutdown handle cancels out in the comparison.

## Testing

- `./check.sh` (io_uring): 563/563
- `-Dbackend=epoll`: 563/563, `-Dbackend=poll`: 562/562
- `./check.sh --target x86_64-windows --wine` (iocp): 499/499
- `x86_64-macos` cross-compile (kqueue): builds
- `./check.sh --full` (examples): passes

## Follow-up (custody handover PR)

- `sockreg.park` hands full completion custody to the fd's owner loop: repoint `completion.loop` and move the active count under the shard lock; `detach` reclaims both on a cancel win. Cancel routing then converges on the servicing thread.
- epoll/kqueue inflight becomes per-instance (how many ops THIS poller is responsible for producing) instead of group-shared, transferred at the same park/detach points. A loop with nothing parked then correctly skips the poll syscall instead of polling because some other loop has work.


## Bug fix: cross-thread clearTimer racing a firing timer (second commit)

A fired timer sits in a limbo window (removed from the heap and result set under the timer lock, `markCompleted` after unlock, state still `.running`). A cross-thread `Loop.clearTimer` in that window corrupted the timer heap, double-decremented `active`, and cleared the result `markCompleted` asserts on. On main the double decrement panics (plain `active -= 1` underflow); this PR's atomic counter would have silenced that symptom while leaving the corruption, so the fix belongs here. Under the lock, `.running and has_result` now unambiguously means mid-fire and `clearTimer` leaves the timer alone; `cancelLocal` sets its result inside the lock and `Loop.setTimer` drops stale results on rearm to keep the invariant exact. A regression test reproduces the original crash reliably with the guard reverted. Cherry-pickable onto main if a hotfix release is needed before this PR merges.

Ports `picard.sam.GatherBamFiles` at tag 3.4.0 for its block-copying fast path.

## What it does

When every input is a BAM file (`determineBlockCopyingStatus`), the tool calls `BamFileIoUtils.gatherWithBlockCopying`, concatenating the inputs by copying their compressed blocks (first file's header kept, the rest dropped) rather than re-encoding.

The block copy is `htsjdk_bam::gather_bam_files`, landed and **proven byte-identical to htsjdk's `gatherWithBlockCopying`** in htsjdk-rs #37 (5 oracle cases, including empty-first, empty-middle, and 3000-reads-per-file many-block). So this tool is a pass-through and byte-identity against Picard with `USE_JDK_DEFLATER=true` holds transitively — unit tests only, no new Picard oracle (the light transitive-proof pattern, as AddCommentsToBam #65).

The `gatherNormally` re-encode path (any input a SAM or CRAM) and `CREATE_INDEX` / `CREATE_MD5_FILE` are deferred. Pin bumped to htsjdk-rs `b4f3fbd`. Unit tests green, clippy + fmt clean.
